purpose: The countable lists. Every entry here is finite and nameable, and every one is something a drawing can be checked against without measuring a distance. Proportions and measurements are deliberately absent -- they live in the prose, because a measured quantity was repeatedly misread in this project while a countable list was not.

body_parts.source: Hampton, Figure Drawing: Design and Invention, p10. 'It is important to be aware that you are describing the eight parts of the body.'
body_parts.note: Listed one per side so that the count matches the list. Hampton writes them as pairs -- arms (2), legs (2) -- which makes six names for eight parts, and a list whose length disagrees with its own count is the one kind of error this file must not contain.

line_kinds.source: Hampton p10. 'In this drawing process, you will never use any other type of line.'

drawing_stages.source: Hampton p35: looking for the skeleton is 'the second stage ... a transitional stage in developing volume'. Bradley's book adds detail and colour on top; Ishiwatari's thirteen-step pipeline splits the same whole into four of line and seven of colour.

fold_types.source: Bradley, Drawing People: How to Portray the Clothed Figure, ch.13.

causes.pipe: fabric falls freely from a condensed area; semicylindrical or semiconical
causes.zigzag: the inside of a bend in tubular cloth buckles; the stiffer the fabric the more angular
causes.spiral: tubular cloth condensing around a tubular form; the softer the fabric the rounder

face_parameters.source: More How To Draw Manga vol.4, Mastering Bishoujo Characters, p11: twelve types given as six opposed pairs.
face_parameters.note: These say who the character is, not whether the drawing is accurate. The eye-to-mouth distance being short is what makes a face read as a child's.

face_parts_for_combination.source: Tezuka, How to Draw Manga, p40: a table of four parts by eight variants, combined.
face_parts_for_combination.note: A face is built by combining parts, not by measuring one.

value_layers.source: comic-inking, ch.V. Objects beside each other but on different planes must not share a value.
value_layers.diagnostic: squint: a flat grey blur means a black and a white are missing

contour_jobs.source: comic-inking, ch.IV. Depth rule: heavy contour on the foreground, medium on the middle ground, fine on the background.

items: cursive (heaviest at the middle of a stroke)
angular or terse (heaviest at the end)
dead-weight (bold contour with fine interior detail)
contour_styles.source: comic-inking, ch.IV. Weights of a kind must agree with each other -- thin lines all alike, heavy lines all alike.

light_source_rule.summary: heavy line weight on the dark side of an object, thin on the light side

hair_rule.light_hair: cursive and elegant lines, weight set by the primary light source
hair_rule.dark_hair: follow the white highlight patterns; the negative space defines the hair's shape

three_dimensions_device.summary: draw an imaginary sphere around the subject and use it as the pivot; the camera, the light and the point of view all sit on that sphere
three_dimensions_device.source: Imagine FX Presents Anatomy vol.2, p62 (Ron Lemen). 'The circle is really a sphere. Ellipses with the long axis passing through circles center point.'

process_rule.summary: a rough sketch is a formal step: loose lines first, expressing the movement and the outline of the story, then inking and cleaning up, with the detail given by the variation of the line
process_rule.source: Super Anime Show 3: A Quick Study Book of Manga Sketching, ch.1-2

items: do not measure slowly -- 'the downside to slowly measuring out the figure is that it stiffens the poses' (Hampton p10)
do not let a stable symmetrical pose stand -- 'the action has either not begun, or it has ended' (Hampton p26)
do not use right angles -- 'organic shapes do not contain right angles' (comic-inking ch.VI)
do not overuse cross-hatching -- 'excessive cross-hatching is not a sign of artistic skill' (comic-inking ch.VII)

expression_layers.source: MEDIBANG, 'how to draw a deformed character's facial expression' by Tsukasan, 2021.11.21
expression_layers.note: The article starts from one face with only the eyes, mouth and brows changed, and says that is not enough. Manpu are sweat drops and anger marks; posture means a laughing person holds the belly; the parts means ribbons and hair move with the emotion -- 'for anger I made the ribbon and hair sharp like horns'. So hair, ribbons and ornaments are part of the face's work.

picture_pipeline.source: MEDIBANG, 'let us finish one picture for now' by NAKAI Nobu, 2021.12.01
picture_pipeline.note: Two rules from the same article: draw at a larger size than the finished picture will be shown and shrink it afterwards, so the drawing can be rough; and recolouring the line art is described as the only way to make a picture look elegant.

items: 1bpp (black and white only, for printed line art)
8bpp (white through grey, for coloured line art and screentone)
layer_weights.source: MEDIBANG, 'let us finish one picture for now'

pose_elements.source: CLIP STUDIO digital-art, 'using guide lines to grasp dynamics and put a soul into a pose', by Eridey
pose_elements.note: These are called the elements that do not change with style. One anti-rule sits beside them: too many action lines scatter the forces and the eye cannot settle on the most important movement, so the count is one to three, never many.

fold_material_axes.source: CLIP STUDIO digital-art, 'drawing folds by fabric: T-shirt, hoodie, shirt, suit', by miyuli
fold_material_axes.note: Folds have no fixed shape of their own; the material decides where they land and how wide they are, and they are pulled toward the seams.

items: one large in front, one small behind
composition_methods.source: MEDIBANG, 'let us think about the composition of an illustration', 2021.07.14, and 'how to place several people', 2021.03.29
composition_methods.note: The rule of thirds is the one stated with a failure case: the subject goes on one of the four intersections, and a picture whose subject sits nowhere near them leaves the viewer unable to tell what to look at. Composition is worked out on the greyscale silhouette, which is the same device as the chibi silhouette test.

canvas_ratios.source: MEDIBANG, 'let us think about the composition of an illustration'
canvas_ratios.note: Each is given with the pixel size it usually appears at and what it is used for -- 16:9 for video, 4:3 for screens, 3:2 for photographs, 1:1 for avatars.

items: let the subject break the frame
enlarge the part you most want seen
composition_devices.source: MEDIBANG, 'simple composition tips that make an illustration look better', 2021.03.15
composition_devices.note: Two of the four are stated as cause and effect: the eye is drawn to the edged area, so a margin beside the figure pulls the gaze outwards; and a tilted picture reads as unstable and moving where a frontal one reads as stable and still -- which is Hampton's 'stable, symmetrical positions keep the action in stasis' said from the picture's side rather than the body's.

items: divide the head height from crown to chin in two
draw a circle for the cranium
drop a line below the circle by half its radius
draw a vertical through the middle of the circle
drop two verticals from the circle's sides to the jaw line
attach a rectangle to the lower half of the circle -- this box is eyes, nose and jaw
mark the reference line across the circle
divide the jaw line in three
draw the face line using those guides
head_construction_steps.source: MEDIBANG, 'let us draw a front face, basic', 2021.02
head_construction_steps.note: Ten steps rather than the four-quarter circle of the girl-face article. The two agree where they overlap -- the eye line sits in the lower half -- and this one adds the cranium-and-face split, which is the distinction the skull actually has: a brain case and a facial area.

items: place the buildings as a black and white silhouette, no detail
separate each form's light, dark and middle face
pull the tone curve so the darks go darker and the lights lighter
background_steps.source: MEDIBANG, 'beautiful backgrounds using texture', and 'creating cool backgrounds'
background_steps.note: The middle step carries a countable fact: a cube seen as a cube shows three faces, never more, so a form of this kind has exactly three values to find. The background is built the same way as the figure -- silhouette first, then volume, then value -- which is the same order as the three stages.
